clue.text: Rough game stopped early, close to end

indicators.note: a thing stopped early loses its final part, so the last letter of the game goes

parts.note: rugger is the informal British name for rugby union

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, so only the end of this word is taken

explanation.surface: A rough match was abandoned before time, near the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopped early' cuts RUGGER to RUGGE; 'close to' takes the D ending 'end'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugged ground or a rugged face is rough and uneven, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Military uniform for prison guard

parts.note: military affairs are the business of war, as in war office
dress is formal uniform, as in mess dress or full dress

explanation.surface: Army kit is being issued to a warder at a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardress is a female warder, someone who guards inmates in a jail.

clue.text: We like being with the English, also helping out

definitions.text: We like being with the English

indicators.note: out suggests the letters have come out of their usual order and been rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Expatriates say they enjoy English company and lend a hand too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the eleven letters of ALSO HELPING.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglophiles are admirers of England and the English, the people who would say they enjoy their company.

clue.text: Wine regularly consumed by friends

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken, here the even ones of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A bottle of wine that one's friends habitually drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second, fourth and sixth letters of 'friends'.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is a common shorthand for red wine, as in a glass of red.

clue.text: Adjusted speed, going round on foot

indicators.note: going round tells us the rearranged letters surround the other piece
something adjusted has been altered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone changed their pace while walking around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adjusted' makes SPDEE, which goes 'round' the other piece. 'foot' is a metrical foot of verse, not the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A spondee is a metrical unit of two stressed syllables, one of the feet of verse.

clue.text: Member of orchestra: see one facing Solti, playing

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for vide, Latin for see, in references
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are being played with and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Look at a musician sitting opposite conductor Georg Solti during a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges SOLTI to OLIST. Georg Solti was a celebrated conductor, which fits the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A violist plays the viola, a regular string section player in an orchestra.

clue.text: Couriers drop small weights round part of gym?

indicators.note: round says the dropping and weights pieces surround the gym piece

parts.note: to drop something is to ditch it
many gyms include a spa, a health club area with pools and saunas
riders are small sliding weights on the beam of a balance

explanation.surface: Delivery men put down little dumbbells around a section of the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' signals the container. 'weights' tempts toward dumbbells, but riders are the small weights of a precision balance.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispatch riders are motorcyclists who carry urgent messages and parcels, a type of courier.

clue.text: Now artist helps refit light substitute for carpeting?

indicators.note: refit means to fit together again in a new way, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter is now helping to lay new flooring as a cheaper option to carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refit' rearranges NOW ARTIST HELPS. 'carpeting' looks like floor covering, but here it means a scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: A token reprimand is a mild alternative to a severe telling-off, which is what a carpeting is in British slang.

clue.text: Ignore blooming teacher at the front

indicators.note: at the front places the teacher piece before the blooming piece

parts.note: Miss is what pupils call a female teacher
flowers that are blooming are out

explanation.surface: Disregard a flowering schoolmistress standing before the class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blooming' looks like a British mild oath, but it means in flower, OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss something out is to omit or leave it aside, which is to ignore it.

clue.text: Roads winding round, say, African territory

indicators.note: round says the twisted letters surround the next piece
winding suggests the letters twist into a new order

parts.note: lanes are narrow roads
EG, for example, is what say means when introducing an instance

explanation.surface: Twisting highways circle part of a country in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winding' rearranges the roads into SENAL, and 'round' wraps that around the example abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal is a country in West Africa, so it is a territory on that continent.

clue.text: Town where Jane will retire shortly

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the shortened name is read in reverse
shortly says the surname is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: Jane Eyre is the title heroine of Charlotte Bronte's novel

explanation.surface: A place where a woman named Jane plans to move when she stops working soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts EYRE to EYR; 'will retire' turns it round. RYE is a small historic town in East Sussex, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a small town in East Sussex, England, on the coast near Hastings.

clue.text: Doctor enters US ward, calling, first off, for liniment

indicators.note: enters puts the doctor inside the ward

parts.note: ER, the emergency room, is the American name for a hospital casualty ward
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: first off removes the opening letter of the word for calling

parts.note: a vocation is a calling

explanation.surface: A physician walks into an American hospital ward on a call, bringing ointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' signals the container and 'first off' drops the opening letter of the calling.
explanation.definitionFit: An embrocation is a lotion rubbed into the skin to ease aches, the same as a liniment.

clue.text: Flustered boss installs computers etc in this place

indicators.note: installs puts the other pieces inside the boss

parts.note: MD, managing director, is a company boss
IT, information technology, covers computers and the like
here means in this place

explanation.surface: An anxious manager sets up computers right here in the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'installs' signals the container. The answer is northern English dialect for bothered or harassed.
explanation.definitionFit: Mithered is a northern English dialect word for bothered or pestered, close to flustered.

clue.text: Philosopher's excellent, mostly cosy home, after retirement

indicators.note: retirement means going backwards, so the assembled pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: ace means excellent

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is used

parts.note: a nest is a snug home

explanation.surface: A thinker's top-notch, nearly snug house he lives in once he stops working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts NEST to NES, giving ACENES, which 'after retirement' reverses. Seneca was a Roman Stoic thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Seneca the Younger was a Roman Stoic thinker and statesman, adviser to Nero.

clue.text: British will abandon attack here, by the way

indicators.note: abandon means the British letter is left out of the attack

parts.note: a broadside is a forceful attack, here the volley a warship fires

explanation.surface: UK forces are going to give up an offensive at this spot along the route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the way' is not the conversational aside but literally beside the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at the roadside lies along the edge of the route, literally by the way.

clue.text: Funny team, not bottom of division

indicators.note: not means the following letter is excluded

parts.note: a gang is a group or team working together

indicators.note: bottom of a word in a down clue is its last letter

explanation.surface: A comic troupe that is not at the foot of the league table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom of' takes N from 'division'; 'not' removes it from GANG. 'Funny' is used as a noun, a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A funny, used as a noun, is a joke or quip, which is what a gag is.

clue.text: Old men help lifting parts of speech

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife
OR, other ranks, is military shorthand for ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting means the word reads upwards, so it is reversed

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: Veteran servicemen assist in raising sections of an address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' turns AID upwards to DIA. 'parts of speech' looks like grammar's nouns and verbs but means sections of an oration.
explanation.definitionFit: Exordia, plural of exordium, are the opening sections of a speech or treatise.

clue.text: Fan in hotel has blown page here and there

indicators.note: in places the fan inside the rearranged letters
blown suggests letters scattered by the wind into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a lover of something is a fan of it

explanation.surface: An electric fan inside a hotel has scattered a sheet of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blown' rearranges the hotel letters to ALTHESHO and 'in' houses the fan there. 'Fan' looks like the machine but means an enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: All over the shop is a British idiom for scattered everywhere, in every direction.

clue.text: Strident noise from party over road …

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the party above the road piece

parts.note: a disco is a dance party

explanation.surface: A loud din coming from a party across the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Discord is a harsh clash of sounds, a jarring noise in music.

clue.text: … so loud? I'll provide accommodation for sleepers, perhaps

definitions.text: I'll provide accommodation for sleepers, perhaps
definitions.meaning: sleepers are small rings worn in pierced lobes to keep the holes open, so this procedure makes room for them

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the strident noise of 6 down to this clue. 'sleepers' suggests railway sleepers or a hotel, but they are small earrings.
explanation.definitionFit: An ear-piercing noise is so shrill and loud it seems to pierce the ears, and the operation makes holes for earrings.

clue.text: Unexciting night out in Kent area?

parts.note: SE, South East, is the region of England containing the county of Kent
a date is an evening out with someone

explanation.surface: A dull evening's entertainment somewhere in the south-east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in South East England, abbreviated SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate means calm and unhurried, so a sedate affair is quiet and unexciting.

clue.text: Cook, I admitted, does food for top copper

indicators.note: admitted means the letter is let in to the cook

parts.note: a chef is a cook
to do someone is to cheat them, and cons are swindles, so cons means does
table can mean the food served, as in keeping a good table

explanation.surface: A cook confesses to cheating with the meals he serves a senior police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted' puts I in CHEF. 'does' means swindles, CONS; 'food' is TABLE, as in a fine table. In Britain the chief constable heads a police force.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief constable is the head of a British police force, the senior officer, copper being slang for police.

clue.text: Initially offended by smell of fish past its sell-by date?

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letters of the two words that follow

parts.note: sole is a flatfish
a scent is a smell

explanation.surface: A whiff of fish signals produce gone off and beyond the date on its label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' gives O and B from 'offended by'; 'smell of fish' gives SOLE then SCENT, 'of' linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsolescent means going out of use or date, like goods nearing their expiry, the question mark flagging the playful sense.

clue.text: Virgin hunter in Catalan tales

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A maiden huntress appears in stories from Catalonia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the letters spanning 'Catalan tales'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Atalanta was a swift huntress who vowed to stay unmarried, a virgin.

clue.text: Mobile? Its casing is sound

parts.note: a mobile is a cellphone

indicators.note: the casing of a word is its outer letters, here those of the mobile just named

explanation.surface: Is a cellphone's outer cover in good working order?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Its casing' takes the outside letters of 'Mobile', M and E. 'sound' looks like the adjective meaning undamaged, but it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A phoneme is a distinct unit of speech sound in a language.

clue.text: Live with girl, primarily ambitious sort

indicators.note: primarily says these pieces come first, ahead of the living piece

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: Someone moving in with his girlfriend is mostly a social climber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' tells you the with-and-girl pieces lead, ahead of the living verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A wannabe is someone keen to become something, an aspiring or ambitious type.

clue.text: Local theatre director gutted, taken in by American duo

indicators.note: taken in by puts the trimmed director inside the doubled abbreviation
a duo means two of them, so the abbreviation is doubled
gutted means the insides are removed, so only the outer letters remain

explanation.surface: A theatre director was devastated to be fooled by two Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' leaves DR of 'director'; 'duo' gives AMAM; 'taken in by' puts DR in the middle. AM-DRAM is British for amateur dramatics.
explanation.definitionFit: Am-dram is British slang for amateur dramatics, the community theatre of a local group.

clue.text: Single bridge-player holding clubs and diamonds

indicators.note: holding puts the clubs letter between the other two

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one, a single
East is one of the four positions at bridge, abbreviated E
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A lone card player has a hand containing clubs and diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts C between I and E. 'diamonds' looks like a card suit but is slang for gems.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice is underworld slang for diamonds, from their glassy glitter.
